claims.statement: Saved App data needs organization/enterprise provenance in addition to user ID. The SAML employee-departure example shows copied code/analysis can leak after membership removal unless the App enforces current contextual access; initial sign-in is not permanent authorization.

Use durable user IDs rather than mutable handles, organization slugs or email addresses for identity references; also use repository, organization and enterprise IDs. The fragment identifies GET /user but links a get-a-user anchor, requiring endpoint-context reconciliation rather than treating the anchor as equivalent authorization. Durable identity alone does not prove current access.

Track user-token organization authorization over time and regularly query user installations; membership removal or missing SAML sign-in can remove access. Deny App-held organization data while unauthorized, until valid SSO or membership restoration and current access verification. Endpoint data and stable identity do not alone prove every cached-data access path is gated.
